name: Computer Science
description: The theory-to-practice study of computation and software: programming, data structures and algorithms, computer systems (architecture, operating systems, networks, databases, distributed and cloud computing), programming languages, software engineering, security, HCI, graphics and the profession. Theoretical foundations live in Mathematics and AI/ML in its own discipline.

chapters.name: Computational Thinking & Introduction to Computing
chapters.summary: A first look at how computers represent information, run programs and talk to each other, and at the problem-solving habits (decomposition, abstraction, algorithms) behind all of computer science.

topics.name: What computer science is: problems, algorithms and computation
Decomposition, pattern recognition, abstraction and algorithm design
Expressing algorithms with flowcharts and pseudocode
Representing text, images, sound and video as data
Hardware basics: CPU, memory, storage and input/output
Software layers: operating systems, applications and programming languages
How the Internet and the Web work: packets, IP addresses, DNS and HTTP
Everyday algorithms: searching, sorting and comparing their efficiency
Limits of computation: problems computers cannot solve (intuition)
Data, privacy and personal cybersecurity basics
A first program in a block-based language (Scratch)

chapters.name: Programming Fundamentals with Python
chapters.summary: Learn to write, run and debug small programs in Python, the usual first language, covering variables, control flow, functions, core data types and files.

topics.name: Setting up Python, the REPL and a code editor
Loops: while, for and common iteration patterns
Functions: parameters, return values and scope
Errors, exceptions and debugging with print statements and a debugger
Modules, imports and the standard library
Installing packages with pip and using virtual environments
Small projects: text games and data-processing scripts

chapters.name: The Command Line & Developer Tools
chapters.summary: The everyday toolkit of a programmer: the Unix shell, text processing, scripting, remote access, editors and build automation.

topics.name: The terminal, the shell and the filesystem hierarchy
Navigating and manipulating files: ls, cd, cp, mv, rm, find
Text processing with grep, sed, awk, sort and cut
Shell scripting: variables, conditionals, loops and functions
Processes and job control: ps, kill, signals and background jobs
Package managers (apt, Homebrew, winget) and installing tools
Remote machines: SSH, keys, scp and rsync
Text editors: Vim basics and a modern IDE (VS Code)
Overview of debugging and profiling tools

chapters.name: Version Control with Git
chapters.summary: How to track, share and merge changes to code with Git and hosted platforms such as GitHub, the basis of all collaborative software work.

topics.name: Why version control: history, collaboration and reproducibility
Git's data model: blobs, trees, commits and refs
Remotes: clone, fetch, pull and push
Undoing changes: restore, reset and revert
Collaborative workflows: feature branches, pull requests and code review
Hosting platforms: issues, forks and CI integration (GitHub, GitLab)
Power tools: bisect, stash, cherry-pick, submodules and worktrees
Branching strategies and commit conventions (trunk-based, Git Flow)

chapters.name: Discrete Mathematics for Computer Science
chapters.summary: The mathematics every computer scientist uses daily (logic, proofs, sets, counting, number theory and graphs), taught with computing examples.

topics.name: Proof techniques: direct proof, contradiction, contrapositive and cases
Counting: sum and product rules, permutations and combinations
Recurrence relations and how to solve them
Asymptotic notation and growth of functions
Number theory for computing: divisibility, modular arithmetic, gcd and primes
Graphs: paths, connectivity, trees and graph representations

chapters.name: Probability & Statistics for Computer Science
chapters.summary: Probability and statistics as used in computing: random variables, tail bounds, simulation, estimation and testing, with applications to algorithms, systems and data.

topics.name: Sample spaces, events and counting-based probability
Conditional probability, independence and Bayes' theorem
Discrete random variables: Bernoulli, binomial, geometric and Poisson
Continuous random variables: uniform, exponential and normal
Expectation, variance and linearity of expectation
Tail bounds: Markov, Chebyshev and Chernoff
Law of large numbers and the central limit theorem
Sampling, simulation and Monte Carlo estimation
Confidence intervals and hypothesis testing, including A/B tests
Probability in computing: hashing, randomized algorithms and load balancing

chapters.name: Program Design & Intermediate Programming
chapters.summary: Moving from scripts to well-designed programs: specifications, recursion, higher-order functions, data abstraction, testing and systematic debugging.

topics.name: Designing functions from specifications: contracts, examples and tests
Recursion and recursive data such as lists and trees
Data abstraction and abstract data types
Classes and objects as a design tool
Unit testing with a test framework (pytest)
Comparing running times of alternative solutions
Working with data: CSV, JSON and web APIs

chapters.name: Object-Oriented Programming
chapters.summary: Programming with classes, objects, interfaces and polymorphism in a statically typed language such as Java, C# or Kotlin.

topics.name: A statically typed OO language (Java, C# or Kotlin): syntax and toolchain
Lambdas and functional features in OO languages

chapters.name: Functional Programming
chapters.summary: Programming with pure functions, immutable data, algebraic data types and higher-order abstractions, in languages such as Haskell, OCaml or Scala.

topics.name: Higher-order functions: map, filter and fold
Algebraic data types and pattern matching
Lazy evaluation and infinite data structures
Type classes and ad hoc polymorphism
Functors, applicatives and monads for effects
Handling state, errors and I/O functionally
Functional programming in practice: Haskell, OCaml, F#, Scala, Clojure and mainstream languages

chapters.name: Data Structures
chapters.summary: The standard ways to organise data in memory (lists, trees, hash tables, heaps and graphs), their costs, and how to choose between them.

topics.name: Linked lists: singly, doubly and circular
Hash tables: hash functions, chaining and open addressing
Graph representations: adjacency lists and matrices
Standard-library collections: sets, maps and multimaps
Memory layout, cache friendliness and choosing a data structure

chapters.name: Design & Analysis of Algorithms
chapters.summary: The core algorithm-design techniques (divide and conquer, greedy, dynamic programming, graph algorithms) with proofs of correctness and running time, up to NP-completeness.

topics.name: Sorting: merge sort, quicksort, heapsort and the comparison lower bound
Graph search: BFS, DFS, topological sort and strongly connected components
Shortest paths: Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford and Floyd-Warshall
Minimum spanning trees: Kruskal and Prim
Coping with hardness: backtracking, branch and bound, approximation and heuristics

chapters.name: Advanced Algorithms & Data Structures
chapters.summary: Graduate-level algorithm design: randomized, approximation, online, streaming and external-memory algorithms, plus advanced and succinct data structures.

topics.name: Linear programming duality in algorithm design
Advanced search structures: splay trees, van Emde Boas trees and fusion trees
Persistent, retroactive and succinct data structures
Suffix trees, suffix arrays and advanced string algorithms

chapters.name: Software Construction
chapters.summary: Writing code that is safe from bugs, easy to understand and ready for change: specifications, abstract data types, testing, static checking and code review.

topics.name: Designing and testing to a specification
Abstract data types, representation invariants and abstraction functions
Static typing, static checking and linters
Defensive programming, assertions and error handling
Recursive data types in real programs
Grammars, parsers and small domain-specific languages

chapters.name: Object-Oriented Design & Design Patterns
chapters.summary: Principles and reusable patterns for structuring object-oriented code so it stays flexible, testable and understandable as it grows.

topics.name: Design principles: cohesion, coupling, DRY and KISS
Creational patterns: factory, builder, singleton and prototype
Structural patterns: adapter, decorator, composite, facade and proxy
Behavioural patterns: strategy, observer, command, iterator, state, visitor and template method
Dependency injection and inversion of control
Domain-driven design basics: entities, value objects and aggregates
Anti-patterns and when not to use patterns

chapters.name: Software Testing & Quality Assurance

topics.name: Testing fundamentals: faults, errors, failures and the test oracle
Black-box techniques: equivalence partitioning, boundary values and decision tables
Unit, integration, system and acceptance testing
Test doubles: mocks, stubs and fakes
Static analysis, code review and inspections
Software quality models and reliability metrics

chapters.name: Software Engineering Process & Team Practice

topics.name: Software life-cycle models: waterfall, iterative and spiral
Agile methods: Scrum, Kanban and Extreme Programming
Project management: scheduling, risk and tracking
Code ownership, reviews and engineering culture

chapters.name: Requirements Engineering

topics.name: Stakeholders and the role of requirements
Elicitation techniques: interviews, observation and workshops
Requirements modeling: domain models, state machines and sequence diagrams
Formal and semi-formal specification (Z, Alloy, OCL)

chapters.name: Software Maintenance, Refactoring & Evolution

Working with legacy code: seams and characterization tests
API evolution, semantic versioning and deprecation
Migration and modernization of legacy systems
Software analytics and mining software repositories
Large-scale changes and automated refactoring tools

chapters.summary: The high-level structure of software systems: architectural styles, quality-attribute trade-offs, documentation and evaluation of architecture decisions.

topics.name: What architecture is: structures, views and decisions
Quality attributes and trade-offs: performance, availability, modifiability and security
Architectural styles: layered, pipe-and-filter, client-server and event-driven
Monoliths, modular monoliths, service-oriented architecture and microservices

Architecture for cloud and serverless systems

Combinational circuits: multiplexers, decoders, adders and the ALU
Sequential circuits: latches, flip-flops, registers and counters

Assembly programming: registers, arithmetic and branches
Procedures, the stack and calling conventions
Memory hierarchy overview: registers, cache, RAM and disk
Building a computer from NAND gates (Nand2Tetris-style project)

chapters.name: Systems Programming in C

Static and dynamic linking, libraries and loaders
Unix I/O: file descriptors, system calls and buffering
Makefiles and build systems for C projects
Systems projects: a shell, a memory allocator or a cache simulator

Instruction-level parallelism: superscalar and out-of-order execution

topics.name: Role of the OS: abstraction, protection and resource management
Kernel architectures: monolithic, microkernel and hybrid
System calls, traps and user/kernel mode
Processes and the process life cycle
Synchronization: locks, semaphores, condition variables and monitors
Virtual memory: page tables, TLBs and page replacement
File systems: interface, implementation and journaling
